regions.summary: Northern Ningxia: all of Shizuishan prefecture (Pingluo county, Dawukou and Huinong districts) plus the northern third of Helan county.

candidates.name: Shizuishan
candidates.meaning: "Stone-mouth mountain": a rock on the Yellow River bank that juts out like a mouth (山石突出如嘴), first called Shizuizi.
candidates.fit: Very good. The region holds 98.6% of Shizuishan prefecture's people, and the prefecture is 68% of the region. Shizuishan is a prefecture of about 0.75M, not a 1M city.
candidates.recognisability: High: the current prefecture name, and the only city of note in the region.
candidates.source_note: Ningxia civil affairs department place-name series, part 3: the town was named for rocks on the Yellow River bank, "山石突出如嘴", colloquially 石嘴子; recorded 1729; city founded 1960.

candidates.name: Helanshan
candidates.meaning: The Helan Mountains, named after the Helan tribe (贺兰部, Xiongnu or Xianbei); 贺兰 is said to mean "mottled" in Turkic.
candidates.fit: Good. The highest, central part of the range (peak 3,556 m in Helan county) runs along the whole western edge of this region; Shizuishan is described as lying where the Helan Mountains meet the Yellow River. Region 4 touches the low southern end.
candidates.recognisability: High: one of Ningxia's three named mountains (with Liupan and Luoshan), and known for its rock art and wine.
candidates.source_note: "十九之匈奴部落中有一支名'贺兰部'，后部落名变为山名"; "突厥语'贺兰'意为'斑駁'". Shizuishan's own site: "石嘴山市地处贺兰山与黄河交汇处".

candidates.name: Pingluo
candidates.meaning: A softened spelling of Pinglu (平虏), "pacify the raiders", the early-15th-century Ming frontier fort; the county took the name Pingluo in 1724.
candidates.fit: Moderate. The region holds all of Pingluo county (cover 99.9%), but it is only 37% of the region.
candidates.recognisability: Medium: a county name, known within Ningxia.
candidates.source_note: County government history page: "明嘉靖三十年(1551年),改设平虏守御千户所"; "雍正二年(1724年)改平虏守御千户为平罗县". Shizuishan site: "'平罗'由'平虏'转音".

candidates.name: Shahu
candidates.meaning: "Sand Lake": a lake on the edge of desert dunes in Pingluo county, a national 5A scenic area.
candidates.fit: Weak as a geographic fit (one lake of about 10 km² of water), but it lies near the middle of the region and is its best-known landmark.
candidates.recognisability: High within China: one of Ningxia's best-known tourist sites.
candidates.source_note: "沙湖位于平罗县，现为国家5A级旅游景区"; about 50 km², roughly 10 km² of it water and 20 km² desert.

candidates.name: Dawukou
candidates.meaning: From 打硙口, "millstone-cutting pass", a Ming-era pass in a valley of the Helan Mountains.
candidates.fit: Moderate. The district is the urban seat of Shizuishan and is 18% of the region (cover 99.7%).
candidates.recognisability: Medium: known as the city centre of Shizuishan.
candidates.source_note: Same series, part 3: the name comes from "打硙口", a pass in the Helan Mountains where millstones were made, dating to the Ming.

candidates.name: Huinong
candidates.meaning: "Benefit the farmers", taken from the Huinong Canal (惠农渠), finished in 1729.
candidates.fit: Weak to moderate. Huinong district (with the old Shizuishan district merged into it) is about 17% of the region. The canal itself runs from the Qingtongxia area to here, through regions 4, 2 and 1.
candidates.recognisability: Medium: a district name.
candidates.source_note: Series part 14: "县名取自清雍正七年（1729年）竣工的惠农渠，寓意惠济于农"; county created 1 April 1941.

regions.notes: The only settled name visible in the tile is Ordos to the east. facts.json lists a unit "Shizuishan Qū" under Wuhai prefecture: that is the old Shizuishan district, abolished in 2003 and merged into Huinong, so its prefecture is wrong. "Taole" (3%) is a county abolished into Pingluo, and the "Sizhan" city (751,389) is really Shizuishan prefecture's population. If Helanshan goes here, Helan should not be used for region 2.

regions.summary: Western Yinchuan: Xixia district's urban streets, most of Jinfeng district, and the Helan county seat Xigang.

candidates.name: Xixia
candidates.meaning: Western Xia, the Tangut empire (1038-1227) whose capital was at Yinchuan; the district is named after the Western Xia royal tombs west of the city.
candidates.fit: Good. Xixia district's urban streets (贺兰山西路, 宁华路, 朔方路, 西花园, 文昌路, 北京西路) make up about 38% of the region and most of the district's people.
candidates.recognisability: High: the dynasty is widely known, and the tombs became a World Heritage site in 2025.
candidates.source_note: "西夏區因西夏王陵得名"; it was the 新市区 part of Yinchuan's former 新城区, renamed on 1 November 2002.

candidates.name: Jinfeng
candidates.meaning: "Golden phoenix". Yinchuan's nickname is Fengcheng (凤城, Phoenix City), but no source I reached says the district was named after it.
candidates.fit: Moderate. Jinfeng streets make up about 25% of the region; the district is split with region 3.
candidates.recognisability: Medium: a district name, seat of the city government since 2006.
candidates.source_note: The district covers the former 新城 area (新满营, 丰乐堡); the city government moved from Xingqing to Jinfeng in 2006.

candidates.name: Helan
candidates.meaning: Named after the Helan Mountains (from the Helan tribe); the county was called Ningxia county until 1941.
candidates.fit: Moderate. The region holds 61% of Helan county's people, including the county seat Xigang (20% of the region), but Helan is only 24% of the region and the region does not reach the mountains.
candidates.recognisability: Medium to high, but shared with the mountains.
candidates.source_note: "1941年，宁夏县改名贺兰县"; the Helan Mountains form the west of the county.

candidates.name: Xincheng
candidates.meaning: "New City": the Qing Manchu garrison town west of old Yinchuan, around which the 1950s new city was built; Jinfeng and Xixia were once the Xincheng district.
candidates.fit: Good for the area (Xincheng is roughly this region), but the name is generic.
candidates.recognisability: Low outside Yinchuan: Xincheng is a common district name elsewhere (Xi'an, Hohhot).
candidates.source_note: "在新满城一带建设新城", creating a 双城 (twin-city) layout; the wetlands between old and new city were later filled in to form 兴庆区, 金凤区 and 西夏区.

candidates.name: Yuehai
candidates.meaning: Literally "viewing the sea": a large lake and national wetland park in Jinfeng, earlier called Daxihu (大西湖, Big West Lake).
candidates.fit: Weak to moderate: a landmark lake at the northern edge of the region rather than a name for the whole area.
candidates.recognisability: Medium within Yinchuan; searches for 阅海 银川 return the wetland park and the Yuehai Bay business district.
candidates.source_note: 宝湖, 阅海 and 鸣翠湖 became wetland parks; 阅海 is also called 金凤区's "大西湖".

regions.notes: Xixia starts with 西 (west) but is the established name of a dynasty, much like Hebei, so I think it passes the rule; flagging in case it reads as "West Xia" to you. Helan here and Helanshan in region 1 would repeat one another, so pick one.

regions.summary: Old city of Yinchuan: most of Xingqing district (Yuhuangge, Yingulu, Lijingjie, Daxin) and the east of Jinfeng.

candidates.name: Yinchuan
candidates.meaning: Literally "silver river" (川 can also mean plain). Used by early-Qing writers for the Ningxia capital and made the city's official name in 1944.
candidates.fit: Required by your rule: Yinchuan is a city of about 2.5M and this region holds the old city (Xingqing, the 老城, including 玉皇阁北街).
candidates.recognisability: High: the capital of Ningxia.
candidates.source_note: Gives the name as lit. "Silver River"; 2020 built-up area 2,564,918.

candidates.name: Xingqing
candidates.meaning: "Flourishing celebration": Xingqingfu, the Western Xia capital on this site from 1038; now the district holding the old city.
candidates.fit: Good. Xingqing streets and towns make up about two thirds of the region, but by your rule Yinchuan should take this region.
candidates.recognisability: Medium: a district name and a well-known historical name.
candidates.source_note: "因西夏时期的兴庆府而得名"; the district is "即原城区或老城".

candidates.name: Fengcheng
candidates.meaning: "Phoenix City", a traditional nickname of Yinchuan.
candidates.fit: Good for the old city, but it is a nickname of the whole city.
candidates.recognisability: Low to medium; Fengcheng is also a city in Liaoning.
candidates.source_note: Lists the nicknames "凤城" and "塞上明珠".

regions.notes: The tile shows no label, so I take it this is unnamed. It is the old centre of a 2.5M city, so Yinchuan is the expected name; the others are listed only for completeness.

regions.summary: The Yellow River plain south of Yinchuan: Litong (Wuzhong city), Lingwu, Qingtongxia and Yongning.

candidates.name: Lingzhou
candidates.meaning: "Spirit isle": a Han county (191 BC) on an island in the Yellow River that "rose and fell with the water and never sank". Later a major Tang prefecture, where Emperor Suzong took the throne.
candidates.fit: Good. Old Lingzhou stood in today's Litong (the 古城 town) until Ming floods moved it to today's Lingwu, so it covers the two largest parts of the region (31% + 25%).
candidates.recognisability: Medium: a searched "Lingzhou Ningxia" goes straight to Lingwu; known from Tang history.
candidates.source_note: Series part 12 (Lingwu), quoting Yan Shigu: "水中可居者曰州，此地在河之州，随水高下，末尝沦没，故号灵州"; set up 191 BC. Part 16 (Litong): after Ming floods only the name 古城 was left, "即今利通区古城镇".

candidates.name: Wuzhong
candidates.meaning: Named after Wu Zhong, a Ming garrison officer (百户) whose fort became Wuzhongbao (吴忠堡).
candidates.fit: Good. Wuzhong city (Litong) is the largest unit (31%, cover 82%) and the prefecture is 80% of the region. Wuzhong's 1.38M in facts is the prefecture; the city itself is well under 1M.
candidates.recognisability: High: a prefecture city and a Hui centre.
candidates.source_note: Series part 4: "其中一堡由百户吴忠管辖，故得名'吴忠堡'"; name kept until 1950 and then given to the county and city.

candidates.name: Qingtongxia
candidates.meaning: "Bronze Gorge", the Yellow River gorge where, in legend, Yu the Great split the mountain with a bronze axe; now also a county-level city and a dam.
candidates.fit: Moderate. The region holds all of Qingtongxia city (cover 100%), 24% of the region. The gorge is the divide between the Weining plain (region 5) and the Yinchuan plain.
candidates.recognisability: High: the dam, the gorge and the 108 stupas are well known.
candidates.source_note: "大禹以青铜神斧劈山导河"; en.wikipedia also gives lit. "Bronze Gorge".

candidates.name: Lingwu
candidates.meaning: From the Han county Lingwu, named for the Lingwu valley (灵武谷) in the Helan Mountains; read as "majestic and martial" (威灵尚武).
candidates.fit: Moderate. The region holds 87% of Lingwu's people, but Lingwu is 25% of the region. Too close to Lingzhou to use both.
candidates.recognisability: Medium to high: a county-level city, known for jujubes and the Shuidonggou site.
candidates.source_note: "灵武，县名，有谷" (后汉书); "以'威灵尚武'之寓意".

candidates.name: Yongning
candidates.meaning: "Lasting peace".
candidates.fit: Weak. The region holds 90% of Yongning county, but it is only 18% of the region.
candidates.recognisability: Low: a common name (Yongning exists in several provinces).
candidates.source_note: Current county name.

candidates.name: Jinji
candidates.meaning: Literally "gold gathered". Jinjipu (金积堡), now Jinji town in Litong, was the headquarters of the Jahriyya Sufi order under Ma Hualong, besieged by Qing forces 1869-71.
candidates.fit: Weak geographically (one town south of Wuzhong city), but a name with real weight in Hui history for a region that is about half Hui.
candidates.recognisability: Low outside Hui history; I would only use it if you want a Hui historical name here.
candidates.source_note: Jinjipu (金积堡) is "a few kilometers south from today's Wuzhong City", the Jahriyya headquarters; besieged from July 1869, Ma Hualong surrendered January 1871. zh.wikipedia 金积镇 places the town in 利通区.

regions.notes: facts.json gives Lingwu's prefecture as Wuzhong while its towns are listed under Yinchuan; Lingwu moved to Yinchuan in 2002, so the county layer's parent is stale. Lingzhou and Lingwu are near-duplicates: use at most one.

regions.summary: Zhongwei and the Weining plain: Shapotou district (Zhongwei city), Zhongning county and the northern edge of Tongxin.

candidates.name: Zhongwei
candidates.meaning: "Middle Guard": the Ming garrison Ningxia Zhongwei (宁夏中卫), named in 1403.
candidates.fit: Very good. The city proper (Shapotou district) is 47% of the region (cover 99.9%), and the region holds 72% of Zhongwei prefecture (the rest is Haiyuan, in region 6). The 1.07M in facts is the prefecture; the city is about 0.4M.
candidates.recognisability: High: prefecture city, gateway to Shapotou.
candidates.source_note: 1403 (永乐元年) the Ningxia Right Guard was renamed Ningxia Zhongwei, "中卫之名由此而始".

candidates.name: Weining
candidates.meaning: The Weining Plain (卫宁平原), the Yellow River plain from Shapotou to Qingtongxia; the name joins Zhong-wei and Zhong-ning, its two counties.
candidates.fit: Very good. The plain is about 130 km long and 2-10 km wide and almost all of it is in this region; nearly every large town here (滨河, 宁安, 宣和, 文昌, 石空, 新堡) sits on it.
candidates.recognisability: Medium: an established term in Ningxia geography and irrigation, less known outside.
candidates.source_note: Series part 6: "中卫市境内的黄河冲积平原，叫卫宁平原，人口密集". zh.wikipedia 卫宁平原: east end "东止于牛首山青铜峡", about 130 km long. The two-county origin of the name is my reading, not stated in the sources.

candidates.name: Shapotou
candidates.meaning: Literally "head of the sand slope": the great dune running down to the Yellow River at the edge of the Tengger Desert, a national 5A scenic area that gave its name to the district.
candidates.fit: Moderate to good. Shapotou district is 47% of the region; the scenic area itself is a single spot at the western end.
candidates.recognisability: High: one of China's first 5A scenic areas.
candidates.source_note: "因沙坡头旅游景区而定名的有沙坡头区、沙都酒店、沙坡宾馆、沙坡头机场等". The literal meaning is my own reading.

candidates.name: Zhongning
candidates.meaning: Made from the first characters of Zhongwei and Ning'an (宁安, today's county seat) when the county was split off from Zhongwei.
candidates.fit: Moderate. The region holds 99% of Zhongning county, 35% of the region.
candidates.recognisability: Medium: known as China's goji capital.
candidates.source_note: Series part 27: "同意分设新县，取中卫、宁安之首字，命名中宁县".

candidates.name: Mingsha
candidates.meaning: "Singing sand": a Northern Wei county (and later Yuan prefecture) at today's Mingsha town in Zhongning, where sand sounded under people's and horses' feet.
candidates.fit: Moderate. Yuan-era Mingsha prefecture covered much of Zhongning; the Ming Zhongwei garrison covered roughly today's Shapotou and most of Zhongning.
candidates.recognisability: Weak: searches for 鸣沙 are dominated by Dunhuang's Mingsha Shan.
candidates.source_note: "北魏在如今的中宁县鸣沙镇设置鸣沙县"; "人马经过这里的沙子时，沙子会随着脚步发出声音…所以号称'鸣沙'" (citing 隋书 and 元和郡县图志).

regions.notes: The Tengger Desert lies north of the region but is mostly in Inner Mongolia, so I left it out. facts.json files Tongxin under Zhongwei prefecture and Haiyuan under Guyuan, while their towns are listed under Wuzhong and Zhongwei: the town lists are current (since 2004), the county parents are older.

regions.summary: Ningxia's central dry belt: Haiyuan, most of Tongxin, Yanchi, Hongsibao and the north of Guyuan's Yuanzhou district.

candidates.name: Haiyuan
candidates.meaning: From the Yuan-era Hailadu plain and fort (海喇都), shortened to Haicheng; renamed Haiyuan in 1914 because Fengtian already had a Haicheng.
candidates.fit: Good for a county. The region holds 91% of Haiyuan's people, and Haiyuan is the largest unit (31%).
candidates.recognisability: Medium to high: the 1920 Haiyuan earthquake is internationally known.
candidates.source_note: Series part 28: "元朝称海喇都原，置海喇都堡"; "海喇都堡又称海城"; 1914 "因与奉天省海城县重名，遂改为海原县".

candidates.name: Tongxin
candidates.meaning: "Same heart", from 同心同德 (one heart, one mind); the town was called Tongxin in the early Qing. Its folk name was Bangecheng ("half a city") because the Qingshui River washed away a corner of the walls.
candidates.fit: Good. The region holds 73% of Tongxin's people, 25% of the region, and the county seat Yuhai is here.
candidates.recognisability: Medium: a well-known Hui county.
candidates.source_note: Series part 19: "清初名同心城，寓意'同心同德'"; "因被清水河冲毁一角，俗名'半个城'"; named Tongxin county in 1938.

candidates.name: Qingshui
candidates.meaning: "Clear Water River": Ningxia's largest Yellow River tributary, 320 km from Kaicheng (Guyuan) north through Yuanzhou, Haiyuan and Tongxin to Zhongning.
candidates.fit: Good. Its middle course, the longest stretch, runs through the region's main farming corridor (Touying, Sanhe, Wangtuan, Tongxin, Dingtang). The source is in region 7 and the mouth is in region 5. Yanchi in the east is outside its basin.
candidates.recognisability: Medium: a search for 清水河 宁夏 returns this river, but Qingshui is a common name (Qingshui county in Gansu, Qingshuihe county in Inner Mongolia).
candidates.source_note: "向北流经原州区、海原县、同心县、中宁县等县", "在中宁的泉眼山西侧注入黄河", 320 km. Old names "西洛水、高平川水、蔚茹水". chinanews 2025: "宁夏入黄第一大支流".

candidates.name: Luoshan
candidates.meaning: Luo Mountain (大罗山), one of Ningxia's "three mountains" with Helan and Liupan; named after the Tuyuhun people who settled there in the Tang.
candidates.fit: Moderate. The mountain stands near the middle of the region, between Hongsibao and Tongxin, and is the region's only big forested peak. Few people live on it.
candidates.recognisability: Medium: a national nature reserve; Luoshan is also a county in Henan.
candidates.source_note: People's Daily 2024: "罗山有宁夏中部干旱带上唯一的天然水源涵养林"; "黄河、贺兰山、六盘山、罗山，这'一河三山'是宁夏的重要生态坐标". Origin from series part 4: "因唐代吐谷浑部在此安居得名".

candidates.name: Yanchi
candidates.meaning: "Salt ponds": the 20-odd natural salt lakes around the county town, worked since ancient times.
candidates.fit: Weak to moderate. The region holds all of Yanchi (cover 99.9%), but it is 14% of the region, in its far east.
candidates.recognisability: Medium within Ningxia.
candidates.source_note: Series part 18: "因县城周边分布着大小20余个天然盐湖，自古以来盛产食盐，故得名盐池县".

candidates.name: Hongsibao
candidates.meaning: "Red Temple Fort": an early-Ming temple of rammed red earth, then a fort built in 1507; since 1999, China's largest resettlement area for migrants from the dry south.
candidates.fit: Weak to moderate. The district (created 2009) is not separate in the county layer, but its towns (Taiyangshan, Sunjiatan area) fall in this region, perhaps 15% of it.
candidates.recognisability: Medium: known for resettlement and for wine at the foot of Luoshan.
candidates.source_note: Series part 17: "明初有佛寺，用当地红土夯筑而成，故俗称红寺"; "明正德二年（1507年）在其地建堡，命名红寺堡".

regions.notes: No single unit is most of this region, so every county name is a partial fit. Xihaigu (listed under region 7) would fit here too: Haiyuan is one of its three namesake counties, and its broad definition includes Tongxin, Yanchi and Hongsibao. I gave it to region 7 because that region holds two of the three namesakes. The 孙家滩 (8%) town is listed under Litong, but it lies south of Wuzhong city in this region.

regions.summary: Southern Ningxia: Guyuan city, Xiji, Pengyang, Longde and Jingyuan, around the Liupan Mountains.

candidates.name: Guyuan
candidates.meaning: "Secure plateau": 原 is a loess tableland. Ming name, explained either as avoiding the character 故 or "for its strong, defensible terrain". Earlier Gaoping ("high and flat") and Yuanzhou.
candidates.fit: Good. The region holds the city centre and 58% of the Guyuan unit (28% of the region), and 99% of the region is in Guyuan prefecture. The 1.14M in facts is the prefecture; the city is well under 1M.
candidates.recognisability: High: prefecture city and the centre of southern Ningxia.
candidates.source_note: Series part 5: "原即'塬'，是黄土高原的一种地貌名词"; 固原: "一为讳'故'改固；二为'以其地险固因名之'"; 高平镇 436, "地势既高且平，故名"; 原州 524.

candidates.name: Liupan
candidates.meaning: "Six coils": the old road wound through six switchbacks before reaching the top. Anciently called Longshan; Genghis Khan died here in 1227, and Mao wrote a poem about it on the Long March.
candidates.fit: Good. The main peak (Migangshan, 2,942 m) is on the Jingyuan-Longde border and the second peak is in Yuanzhou, all in this region; the range continues south into Gansu.
candidates.recognisability: High across China.
candidates.source_note: "盘道六重始达山顶"; formerly "陇山"; main peak 米缸山 at the 泾源/隆德 junction; "成吉思汗在养伤期间病逝于六盘山"; Mao's 《清平乐·六盘山》.

candidates.name: Xiji
candidates.meaning: A sound-alike of 蓆芨草 (xijicao), the local name for the jiji grass (芨芨草) that grows thickly there; county formed in 1942.
candidates.fit: Good for a county. The region holds 96% of Xiji, the largest unit at 32%.
candidates.recognisability: Medium: known as the last county in China removed from the poverty list (2020).
candidates.source_note: Series part 22: "因境内盛产芨芨草，俗称'蓆芨草'的谐音演变而来"; formed October 1942 from parts of five counties.

candidates.name: Xihaigu
candidates.meaning: A short form made from Xi(ji), Hai(yuan) and Gu(yuan): the mostly Hui, drought-hit hill country of southern Ningxia.
candidates.fit: Moderate. Two of the three namesake counties (Xiji, Guyuan city) are here, about 60% of the region. The broad definition (nine counties) covers this region and region 6 together.
candidates.recognisability: High within China, with its own en.wikipedia article.
candidates.source_note: "是西吉县、海原县和固原县三县县名首字的简称"; broad sense "囊括了固原市原州区、西吉县、隆德县、彭阳县、泾源县，中卫市海原县以及吴忠市同心县、盐池县、红寺堡区9个县区".

candidates.name: Yuanzhou
candidates.meaning: "Plateau prefecture": Northern Wei prefecture from 524, now Guyuan's urban district.
candidates.fit: Moderate. The same area as Guyuan city (58% of it here), so it is an alternative to Guyuan rather than an addition.
candidates.recognisability: Low to medium.
candidates.source_note: "正光五年（524年）改高平镇置原州".

candidates.name: Xiaoguan
candidates.meaning: Xiao Pass, the Han-dynasty fort guarding the northern approach to the Guanzhong plain, often named in Tang frontier poetry.
candidates.fit: Weak geographically (a pass at Wating in Jingyuan, 7% of the region), and some scholars place the pass elsewhere in different periods.
candidates.recognisability: Medium: famous in poetry; searches for 萧关 宁夏 return Guyuan.
candidates.source_note: "西汉又筑萧关（在今泾源县六盘山镇瓦亭村），是关中北面要塞".

regions.notes: Gaoping (高平, Guyuan's Northern Wei name) is sourced but left out because Gaoping is a city in Shanxi. Pengyang (19%) comes from the ancient Pengrong state plus 阳, "north of the river" (series part 25), if you want it.
